react_result.final_narrative_text: The seven-metabolite differential profile implicates a single dominant pathway with striking cross-paradigm agreement: Galactose Metabolism (KEGG:hsa00052 / SMPDB:SMP00043 / MUMM:galactose_metabolism). RaMP multi-DB ORA returned this pathway at ranks 1–2 with an FDR of 4.25e-11 and a fold-enrichment of 1162, driven by four of the seven input metabolites — sucrose (KEGG:C00089), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), galactinol (KEGG:C01235), and glycerol (KEGG:C00116). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently ranked hsa00052 first with a raw p-value of 3.25e-07, confirming the same four metabolites. Mummichog's m/z-based network method ranked galactose_metabolism third (p=3.36e-04), independently reproducing the signal from mass-spectral correlates without requiring ID resolution. The three paradigms — ORA against curated DBs, empirical network activity, and KEGG-specific set enrichment — converge on the same biological interpretation with no conflicting top-pathway calls. Galactinol (α-D-galactosyl-(1→3)-1D-myo-inositol) is the pathway's most specific compound, connecting galactose catabolism to inositol metabolism; sucrose enters as the primary galactose source. Fructose 1-phosphate and D-glucose contribute to the secondary glycolysis signal (RaMP rank 4, FDR 9.77e-05) rather than the primary galactose hit, and deoxycytidine maps to a distant pyrimidine-metabolism pathway (p=0.117). The biological story is therefore one of perturbed galactose and inositol carbohydrate metabolism, with secondary disruption of central glycolytic flux.

RaMP multi-DB ORA returned this pathway at ranks 1–2 with an FDR of 4.25e-11 and a fold-enrichment of 1162, driven by four of the seven input metabolites — sucrose (KEGG:C00089), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), galactinol (KEGG:C01235), and glycerol (KEGG:C00116).
